core_api.py::_accept_loop.ends: open connections are capped at max_connections and a connection leaves the set when it closes; refusal workers are capped at MAX_REFUSAL_THREADS and each ends when its refusal is answered, a burst past either gets a refusal row and a closed socket, so neither count accumulates

core_api.py::_ask.ends: a per-call byte cap on a question; a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_clean.ends: a recursion depth bound on one reply being filtered; deeper values become None, it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_confirmed.ends: pending confirmations are capped per token; each expires after CONFIRM_SECONDS and expired ones are purged when a new one is asked for, or goes when it is used

core_api.py::_label.ends: a per-call byte cut of one source label as it is written into a delivered line; it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_message_params.ends: a per-call byte cap on one message; a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_need_str.ends: a per-call length and control-character check on a caller-supplied id or short string; it ends with the call, nothing accumulates

core_api.py::_need_text.ends: a per-call byte cap on free text (a note, question or reply); a longer one is refused too_large, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_push_params.ends: a per-call byte cap on one pushed note; a longer one is refused too_large and no intent row is written

core_api.py::_read_json.ends: a per-read byte cap on one records file; a larger file reads as None (unknown), nothing is kept

core_api.py::_read_jsonl_file.ends: a per-read byte cap on one records file; a larger file reads only its newest tail and the reply says incomplete, nothing is kept

core_api.py::_rewrite_tokens.ends: a byte cap on the token store (tokens.json); a larger store is refused on read and a write that would exceed it is refused before replacing, so the file stops at the cap; revoking a token removes its row (an unknown token is refused exactly like a revoked one) and the next mint also drops any row still marked revoked, so revoked tokens never use up the store

core_api.py::_subscribe.ends: live subscriptions are capped overall and per token; a subscription leaves the list when its reader closes, is dropped as too slow, or reaches its limit

core_api.py::_take_push_allowance.ends: a per-token rate limit of PUSH_PER_WINDOW notes per window; times older than the window are dropped on each call; on each call every other token's list is also removed when its window is empty or its token is revoked or unknown, so only tokens with a note in the last window keep a list

core_api.py::_tokens_used.ends: a per-call range check on a reported token count; an out-of-range value is refused, nothing is kept

core_api.py::changes_diff.ends: a per-call byte cut of one diff in the reply (truncated says so); the diffs record itself is bounded by its own retention

core_api.py::handle.ends: a per-reply cut of any list longer than LIST_MAX; the reply says incomplete, nothing is kept

core_api.py::offer.ends: a per-subscriber buffer of undelivered events; when it is full the subscriber is marked dropped and closed, which frees its slot and its buffer

core_api.py::readline.ends: a per-line byte cap on one request line; a longer line is refused too_large and the connection closed, the read buffer never exceeds the limit
